scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket response times (2440 tickets): median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Billing tariff change log (billing-db) contains 0 records.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute volume by month: Jun 610, Jul 590, Aug 1180, Sep 1260.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits utility-requested route priority changes, to be executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: 320 accounts were marked with estimated reads in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes.

F-08.statement: route-log lagging_routes query identified 14 routes with below-target completion, sample route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-09.statement: Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected on billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (firmware v4.2).

F-10.statement: Of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 56 had no AMI read received before cutoff (billing_import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED), confirming a minor true MDMS delivery-failure contribution.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is primarily caused by slow or inadequate ticket response/handling, so an AI auto-answer agent would resolve the volume problem.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (e.g., estimate-substitution logic) around August is systematically generating incorrect bills.

H-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI register reads from the vendor (MDMS) are failing to deliver or validate correctly via H-MDMS-BILL, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The manual meter-read handoff from the contracted field service (H-FIELD-BILL) is failing or arriving invalid, causing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTFALL.statement: Insufficient field reading staffing/capacity is causing missed or late manual reads, driving estimate substitution and disputes.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-DEFECT.statement: A defect in how the billing system processes ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads — e.g. tariff application or calculation error — is generating incorrect bills and disputes on accounts with normal reads.

H-AMI-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTI.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as anomalously high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and plausibly also mis-affecting ACTUAL-read bill calculation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route completion for manual-read accounts fell short of target (0.88 vs 0.95) across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a meaningful gap in field read collection during the dispute-surge period; this is a plausible but not yet confirmed contributor to estimate substitution.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carried an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) an ESTIMATED read, so a majority of disputed bills were not estimate-substituted at all. This means causes that act only through estimate substitution (field handoff/staffing, MDMS delivery) can at most explain the minority ESTIMATED share, pointing toward a billing-side error (e.g., rule/tariff logic) affecting ACTUAL-read bills too.

CRM data shows dispute ticket handling is well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA) across 2440 tickets, indicating response speed/adequacy of ticket handling is not the driver of the Aug-Sep surge. This points the problem away from "slow response" and toward why bills are wrong in the first place.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged in that system. This rules out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism behind the ACTUAL-read billing errors, narrowing (but not eliminating) the billing-defect hypothesis to non-tariff calculation or import logic.

CRM monthly dispute counts jump from ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming the timing and roughly-doubling magnitude of the surge described in the initial request. This is a volume/timing confirmation only; it says nothing about which upstream mechanism (billing, field reads, AMI, rule change, response speed) is causing the wrong bills.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; as a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it corroborates, but does not independently confirm, the authoritative E-04 finding that the tariff change log shows zero records.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative interview) attributes late manual-read routes to being short three readers since July, framing this staffing gap as the mechanism producing estimated bills for affected customers. This is a stakeholder claim about mechanism, not a tool-confirmed count of estimated bills or staffing records.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) establishes that the utility may request route priority changes but they are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD), formally grounding the already-modeled K-DISPATCH human-approval control for push_route_update; it says nothing about the billing-defect causal chain.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: A new billing-db query (accounts_estimated_last_cycle) returns 320 accounts with estimated reads in the most recent cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes; it only carries account_id and route fields, with no dispute status, read-type comparison, or causal attribution, so it establishes a scale figure for current estimate substitution without confirming why those reads were estimated.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), providing route-level granularity on which manual-read routes are below target, consistent with the aggregate 88% completion figure already in E-01, but it carries no staffing or causal attribution for why those routes lag.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside has now been provisioned per vendor ticket TX-4471, which if true would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query, but it is an unverified claim, not a confirmed tool-level status change.

Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-02), all 1240 trace to the AMI channel in MDMS: 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read received before cutoff that was rejected on billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and only 56 (4.5%) truly had no read received. This shows a billing-side import validation rule (not field staffing or MDMS delivery failure) is the dominant mechanism forcing estimate substitution on these disputed accounts, and it also confirms the mdms-export tool is now live and returning authoritative data.

U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.question: Which specific billing-side mechanism (import validation rule change vs. calculation defect) is producing incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts?
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation is a rule-change rollback, a calculation-logic patch, or another billing-import fix; no bill correction should be attempted until this is confirmed.
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes correlating with the Aug 2026 onset and cross-check against ACTUAL-read disputed bill detail (DA-BILL).
U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic data collection only; do not attempt any bill correction until the mechanism is confirmed against billing-config evidence.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: What do AMI register read events for the ESTIMATED-read disputed accounts show, and could MDMS vendor delivery issues be an additional contributor?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Could reveal a secondary AMI/MDMS delivery contributor to the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes; affects whether vendor access must be escalated before closing the investigation.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Vendor (Telemetrix AMI) must provision mdms-export access; the tool is currently DEGRADED (ACCESS_PENDING, recovery HOLD with no fallback) and should be retried once access is granted.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db, route-log, billing-config and crm-tickets diagnostics without MDMS data; treat the ACTUAL-read billing defect as the primary line of investigation until MDMS access is restored.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: MDMS AMI read events for all 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts are now visible: 1184 show billing-import rejection of a received high-consumption read, 56 show genuine non-receipt, so MDMS vendor delivery issues are only a minor (4.5%) contributor.

U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the below-target route completion (88% vs 95%, E-01) actually caused by the three-reader staffing shortfall, or by another field-side issue not yet evidenced by a tool source?
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Affects whether any eventual field-route remediation targets staffing or a different field-side fix; does not change the primary billing-defect finding.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-check route-log completion detail against field staffing records, since SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-07/CL-03) is a non-authoritative stakeholder statement.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the route completion shortfall as a minor, ESTIMATED-read-only contributor and do not reprioritize routes until root cause is confirmed.

proposal.summary: Lakeside Water's dispute-ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). Investigation found 59% of disputed bills carried normal ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED ones (E-02), ruling out a slow-response explanation (E-03) and a tariff change (E-04, E-06), and pointing to a billing-side import/validation defect as the majority driver, with field route under-completion (E-01) and an AMI high-consumption-rejection rule (E-12) explaining most of the minority ESTIMATED share. The release delivers three read-only query capabilities (disputed-bill detail, route completion, dispute-ticket review) as RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, while the one action that could pinpoint the exact billing-rule defect (querying the DA-RULES change log) and the MDMS export-access request are withheld because two verification obligations about them are still open.
key_points: Root problem as defined: dispute volume roughly doubled (E-05); 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry ACTUAL reads versus 41% ESTIMATED (E-02), so the majority cause is a billing import/validation defect, not estimate substitution.
Tariff change was ruled out as a cause: the billing tariff change log has zero records (E-04), corroborated by stakeholder claim (E-06).
Slow ticket handling was ruled out: median response 1.6 days / p90 2.8 days versus a 3.0-day SLA (E-03), so an auto-answer agent would not address the actual driver.

Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills, 1184 (95.5%) had an AMI read that was received before cutoff but rejected on billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and only 56 had no read at all (E-12), showing even the ESTIMATED-read minority is largely a billing-side rejection issue, not field or MDMS delivery failure.

Field route completion for manual reads was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts (E-01), and staffing shortfall is a stakeholder claim (E-07) consistent with but not proven to cause that gap.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; released scope covers query_disputed_bill_detail:DA-BILL, query_route_completion:DA-ROUTE, and review_dispute_tickets:DA-TICKET, all read-only queries with no automated bill writes (consistent with K-BILLWRITE / SC-NO-AUTOMATED-BILL-WRITES).

The core root-cause query, query_rule_change_log:DA-RULES, is excluded because it is blocking_scope under the still-open VOB-U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM; the MDMS export-access request is excluded because VOB-R-2 (whether vendor access per ticket TX-4471 is truly live) remains open with a prior NOT_TRANSIENT HOLD and no fallback path.
The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the deferred verification items tracked as the two open VOBs that now constrain the release scope.
limitations_explained: The specific billing-side mechanism causing wrong ACTUAL-read bills has not been confirmed; the query that could confirm it (DA-RULES change log) is withheld pending resolution of VOB-U-BILLING-DEFECT-MECHANISM, so released queries operate without that confirmation.

Whether MDMS export access is actually live is unresolved (VOB-R-2 open); the request_mdms_export_access action is omitted from release, so cross-validation of ESTIMATED-read disputes against AMI data stays limited.
Upstream data health is uncertain: billing-config tool health is UNKNOWN, so even the released queries may rest on incomplete upstream data.
Even if remedied, field-staffing fixes and MDMS-access fixes would only address the 41% ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes, not the 59% ACTUAL-read majority that drives the surge.

Fixing the actual billing-rule defect once identified would require manual bill correction through SH-BILL's billing_adjustments_manual authority (K-BILLWRITE forbids automated writes), and this corrective work is explicitly unfinished/out of release scope.

Two success criteria tied to root-cause confirmation and dispute-volume restoration (SC-BILLING-DEFECT-IDENTIFIED, SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-RESTORED) cannot be assessed yet because the defect-confirming query is deferred.
